questions.stem: Why does the Haber process use high pressure (200 atm)?

options.text: Because high pressure increases the rate but decreases the yield
Because there are fewer moles of gas on the product side, so high pressure shifts equilibrium towards more ammonia
Because high pressure is needed to keep the iron catalyst working
Because high pressure lowers the activation energy

questions.explanation: In the Haber process (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃), there are 4 moles of gas on the left and 2 moles on the right. High pressure shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer gas moles (the right), producing more ammonia and increasing the yield.
